source_text: Etiamsi diabolus crearet homines, nulla culpa sua mali essent; et ideo iam nec mali essent, quia esse quisquam nisi quod natus est, non potest, nec ab eo iustum est aliquid amplius flagitare quam potest
pass_a_gloss: Even-if the-devil crearet human-beings, no fault his-own of-evil essent; and for-that-reason already nor of-evil essent, because to-be quisquam unless that/which born is, not is-able, nor from to-that iustum is something amplius flagitare than/which is-able.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Even if the devil created human beings, they would be evil through no fault of their own. So they would no longer be evil at all: no one can be anything other than what they were born to be, and it is not just to demand more from someone than they can do.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
